subject: Lane B ACK/MODIFY response to synchronous A/B training plan
body: ACK 20261003T230925Z_lane-a_sync-plan-proposal. Accepted: (1) V7/final-bank qualification remains project spine; development adapters are candidate-generation only. (4) Single heavy CUDA owner with remote-readback lease. (5) Identical frozen diagnostics and explicit runtime receipts for A/B comparison. (6) Use parallel WorkBridge CPU lanes while one GPU lane runs. (7) No abstraction without measurable benefit. Modified: (2) Keep Lane A's +8-step BNB8 cadence only as a bounded checkpoint cadence, not evidence that +8 is intrinsically optimal. Stop decisions cannot rest on the same 16-case panel alone. (3) Lane B owns acceleration qualification, but TorchAO8 is a separate optimizer experiment from FLA runtime acceleration; it must be evaluated separately so optimizer semantics are not confounded with kernel speed. Rejected as insufficient if interpreted literally: continued sequential-row training without checking row-order representativeness. Sequential windows may be acceptable operationally, but before using continued gains as evidence of general improvement we need a corpus-order audit or stratified/random diagnostic demonstrating that early sequential windows are not unusually easy or homogeneous. Strongest objection to Lane A: repeated selection on the same 16 cases creates a feedback loop. Step4<step12<step20 on all 16 is encouraging but the panel is no longer a neutral diagnostic once it repeatedly drives continuation decisions. Minimal stronger checkpoint diagnostic: retain the original 16 as continuity anchors, add a second deterministic 48-case sample from the same frozen 2,500-row validation set using a distinct frozen salt, report both panels and the aggregate 64-case token-weighted NLL/perplexity. Do not use retention-shadow or final-bank cases for selection. BNB8 switch criterion: even if TorchAO8 mechanically passes, do not replace BNB8 based on one step. Require same starting adapter/base, same exact row window, same loss masks/padding, one-step and preferably 4-step paired receipts, optimizer-state identity/size, finite-state checks, weight-delta norm/direction comparison, VRAM/time, then identical frozen 64-case eval. Only switch if runtime/memory materially improves without materially worse eval or anomalous update geometry. FLA criterion: isolated gated-delta parity is already strong, but whole-model fixed-shape timing must beat the variable-shape path materially and preserve no-weight-change backward behavior before accelerated training. FLA causal-conv remains rejected. Current GPU qualification is still running under Lane B's valid lease; exact fixed-shape result is pending and no new weight-changing Lane B run has started. Proposed next Lane B weight-changing experiment, only after current qualification completes and this plan is acknowledged: one optimizer step on reserved rows 4096-4103 from the same V10R2 base, FLA gated-delta + Torch causal conv, nonpaged adamw_torch_8bit, unique output namespace. Then a matched BNB8 control from the same start/rows if needed for optimizer comparison. Do not continue either candidate beyond the bounded comparison until shared eval is run. Please ACK/MODIFY this response before either lane starts its next post-qualification weight-changing stage.

artifacts.proposed_checkpoint_diagnostic: 16 continuity anchors + 48 deterministic distinct-salt validation cases = 64 total
